newsitem.title: JAPAN: Former Prudential manager held in Japan fraud case.
newsitem.headline: Former Prudential manager held in Japan fraud case.

text.p: Police said on Monday they had arrested a former executive of the Japanese subsidiary of Prudential Securities Inc of the United States on suspicion of embezzling 1.13 billion yen ($10.1 million).
Prudential Securities (Japan) Ltd last week accused Atsumi Kikuchi, 37, a former assistant general manager, of obtaining the money through illegal bank transactions.
It said he took a similar amount by pocketing shares entrusted to the firm by customers, and that the total he had embezzled was 2.2 billion yen ($19.8 million).
No charge has yet been brought by police concerning the allegations over the shares. The company said it had already purchased an equal amount of shares on the market and returned them to customers.
On Thursday, the company confirmed Japanese media reports that it had asked Tokyo police to bring charges against a former executive it suspected of embezzlement.

Charles Perkins, senior vice president in charge of public affairs at Prudential Securities Inc, said on Thursday that the loss had been wholly covered by an insurance policy and had not had any impact on the company's performance.
Prudential said it reported the loss to police in July 1995 and in April this year asked for legal action against the man.

Prudential Securities (Japan) was licensed to operate in Japan in late 1979. It relinquished its membership of Tokyo Stock Exchange for trading Japanese shares in the spring of 1995, and its seat was sold to Smith New Court Securities (Japan) Ltd, a unit of Smith New Court Plc.
